title: Fall of Kabul
summary: On 15 August 2021 the Taliban entered Kabul and seized control of Afghanistan's capital after President Ashraf Ghani fled the country. The Afghan government's collapse surprised US officials, and a mass airlift followed, evacuating more than 123,000 people by the end of August. The Doha Agreement of 2020 is argued to have contributed.

as_recorded.value: on 15 August 2021, the Taliban seized control of Afghanistan’s capital, Kabul

importance.justification: Collapse of a US-backed government and end of the 20-year US war, with major humanitarian consequences.

audience_note: Mentions civilian deaths from a suicide bombing and a mistaken airstrike, and Taliban repression.

sources.title: Diplomacy of Disaster: The Afghanistan ‘Peace Process’ and the Taliban Occupation of Kabul in: The Hague Journal of Diplomacy Volume 17 Issue 1 (2022)
United States Grapples with Aftermath of Withdrawal from Afghanistan | American Journal of International Law | Cambridge Core

reviewer_note: Sources are journal articles about the diplomacy and US aftermath, not a narrative of the fall itself. The evacuation figures differ slightly (roughly 120,000 versus more than 123,000). Place coordinates are inferred from the city name only.
